messages:
anna_sales: POC with Acme in 30m — they can't correlate requests across services. Their logs lack a request id and trace export to Datadog isn't wired. Need eng help to enable X-Request-ID propagation + a quick DD dashboard. cc @jenna_solutions @mohit_eng
jenna_solutions: On it. Are they on Hosted or Dedicated?
mohit_eng: Hosted API? That affects how we toggle tracing.
anna_sales: Hosted. They're hitting lots of parallel calls, seeing 429s and responses don't echo X-Request-ID.
mohit_eng: Do you have a sample request/response header pair? Also do they send X-Request-ID or expect us to generate one?
anna_sales: Sample request: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' -H 'X-Request-ID: 8a3f7d' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
anna_sales: They say our responses don't echo X-Request-ID and Datadog logs have no request_id field.
kyle_devops: Probable ingress mapping issue. We should ensure ingress copies X-Request-ID into our access logs and that the forwarder maps it to `request_id`. Example nginx config: ```proxy_set_header X-Request-ID $http_x_request_id;```
mohit_eng: Also ensure runtime tracing middleware is enabled so structured logs include `trace_id` and `request_id`. For Hosted we can enable per-org with `enable_request_tracing=true`.
anna_sales: How quickly can we enable that for a single customer? It's blocking the demo.
jenna_solutions: We can flip a per-API-key flag in staging. If you give me the trial key I'll enable tracing and point their logs at a temporary forwarder.
mohit_eng: If you share org id + key I'll enable tracing and wire a temporary forwarder to their Datadog intake. We'll also extract X-Request-ID into the log schema.
anna_sales: Org: acme-inc, key: rt-ACME-TRIAL-123. They also want a dashboard showing 429s grouped by request_id and latency per request_id. Do we have a template?
kyle_devops: I have a quick Datadog dashboard skeleton. Will sanitize then paste. Minimal: timeseries for status:429, logs table grouped by `request_id` with avg/max latency, and a heatmap for request distribution. Example snippet (skeleton): ```{
  "widgets": [
    {"type":"timeseries","query":"logs(\"status:429 AND source:api\").rollup('count')"},
    {"type":"log_stream","query":"logs('source:api').index('main').group_by('request_id')"}
  ]
}```
observability-bot: Log-forwarder created: ff-12345, destination: https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/acme, status: provisioning (expected delay ~30s) :rocket:
mohit_eng: Forwarder up. Note: rate limiter still enforces 429s — we can add header `X-Rate-Limit-Policy` explaining limit and also temporarily bump limits for trials.
jenna_solutions: Bumped trial limits: per-minute 60 -> 300 for acme-inc for 1 hour. Monitoring.
anna_sales: They're testing now.
acme_engineer: Testing now — I see X-Request-ID echoed in response headers and some logs show request_id, but dashboard still shows many entries without request_id (looks like older services not forwarding header).
mohit_eng: Likely svc-batcher/proxy is stripping headers. I'll run the internal check script and patch proxy config. Runbook: `./runbooks/check-proxy-headers.sh acme-inc svc-batcher`
mohit_eng: curl test to internal svc: ```curl -v -H 'X-Request-ID: test-123' http://svc-batcher.service.internal/health```
acme_engineer: Found svc-batcher not forwarding header, patched to add `proxy_pass_header X-Request-ID` and redeployed. Re-testing.
acme_engineer: All good now — logs show `request_id` for requests and dashboard groups correctly. 429s dropped after rate bump. Thanks everyone :tada:
anna_sales: Awesome. Next actions: make X-Request-ID echoing default for Hosted and add docs. @jenna_solutions can you own the docs + attach dashboard JSON?
jenna_solutions: Yep. I'll add a short guide 'Request ID propagation & observability' and include the sanitized Datadog dashboard JSON and a quick troubleshooting checklist. ETA EOD.
